summary.headline: Minda Corporation Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 1,846 crore (+33.2% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 212 crore at an 11.5% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 33.2% YoY to INR 1,846 crore, up 8% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 212 crore (11.5% margin, +19 bps YoY). PAT of INR 206 crore included a one-time exceptional gain of INR 106 crore from consolidating Minda VAST. Associate Flash Electronics grew revenue 42% YoY to INR 533 crore but its EBITDA margin dipped to 15.4% on commodity and labour costs. Management said the quarter was margin-pressured by raw material, freight and wage inflation, with pass-through mechanisms expected to recover it over one to two quarters.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 533 crore (+42% YoY), EBITDA INR 82 crore at 15.4%; about 30% of Flash revenue from EV with about 90% YoY EV growth. Around 10% of Flash revenue is international (Germany, Hungary), with exports 12-15%.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22% YoY in the quarter; margin 8.4% vs 6.5% a year earlier. Kit value about INR 8,000-13,000 per vehicle.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guidance of about INR 400 crore across business verticals, not allocated specifically to EV or ICE.
Flash Electronics growth target of 20-24% YoY; long-term Flash EBITDA margin 16-17%.
Group EBITDA margin expected at 11.5-12% for the rest of FY27; long-term target 12.5% by 2030 (FY25 about 11.7%).
Vision 2030 reiterated: INR 17,500 crore revenue target supported by existing business growth, premiumisation, exports, new products (about INR 4,600 crore) and inorganic opportunities.
Switches order (lifetime order book above INR 1,000 crore): SOP expected in Q1 FY28; about INR 150 crore revenue in FY28 and peak in FY29.
Turntide motor controller SOPs expected in October-November 2026.
Sunroof business (Spark Minda HCMF) SOP on track for Q2, product trials approved first time.
Flash margin dip expected to reverse in one to two quarters as indexation with customers aligns.
Furukawa share of profit (17.5% holding) expected to be temporary dip.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance about INR 400 crore, spread across verticals and divisions, not specific to EV.
Group capacity utilisation about 77-80% depending on plant or product line.
Investment of INR 63 crore into group companies in Q1 (Spark Minda Green Mobility Solutions, Spark Minda HCMF for sunroofs, Spark Minda Toyo Denso for switches).
Die casting for Flash in partnership with Minda started in August 2026 (first Flash-Minda cross-sell line).
Turntide production set up, lines being tested; SOPs October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: Industry production up about 22% YoY in Q1 FY27 (highest-ever Q1); two-wheelers +23%, passenger vehicles +17%, three-wheelers +39%, commercial vehicles and tractors about +15% each.
EV penetration about 10.6% in two-wheelers and 7.5% in passenger vehicles; EV two-wheeler registrations crossed 5 lakh in a quarter.
Input cost pressure from raw materials, freight, logistics, manpower and wages; most index-linked commodities have back-to-back pass-through with customers, with a lag of a quarter or two.
Order wins spread across vehicle access, castings, wiring harness, clusters and new energy and electronics, across ICE and EV, two-wheeler, PV and CV, domestic and export.
Export order book about 8-10% of total order book.
Flash domestic/international split: about 90% India, 10% international.

qa_highlights.question: Raghunandhan NL (Nuvama): How will order ramp-ups in clusters and wiring harness support FY27 and FY28 sales, and what categories were the Q1 order wins in?
qa_highlights.answer: Wiring harness grew more than 30% YoY and instrument cluster more than 35% YoY in Q1, with momentum expected to continue into FY28. Q1 order wins spanned vehicle access, castings, wiring harness, clusters and new energy/electronics, across ICE and EV, two-wheeler, PV, CV, domestic and export, described as evenly split.

qa_highlights.question: What were Minda VAST's revenue and EBITDA in Q1, and what are its growth and margin prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: VAST revenue grew 22% YoY, lifting group passenger vehicle share from 15% to 19% with consolidation. Margin was 8.4% vs 6.5% in Q1 FY26. Kit value is about INR 8,000-13,000 per vehicle, with products under development that could lift it, spread across PV OEMs in India and exports to Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Can Flash grow 30% for the full year given EV demand, and what margin is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-24% YoY growth for Flash, citing the need to build capacity first. Long-term Flash EBITDA margin is expected at 16-17%, with the Q1 dip attributed to labour and commodity inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex guidance and its EV vs core split? What are the Turntide SOP timing and utilisation? How does group margin compare with peers, and can contract labour help?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 400 crore, not allocated specifically to EV or ICE. Turntide SOPs are expected in October-November 2026, with lines being tested. Group capacity utilisation is about 77-80%. Management said the group is in the first quartile of the industry and guided group EBITDA of 11.5-12% for the rest of FY27, with 12.5% targeted by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Kumar (Narnolia): Is there a revenue shortfall of INR 3,000-3,500 crore against the FY30 target, and what levers close it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the estimate and reiterated INR 17,500 crore by FY30 from existing business growth, premiumisation, exports, new products (about INR 4,600 crore) and inorganic opportunities. It said organic growth is tracking about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did Minda VAST merger add, and what was the Q4 FY26 VAST margin? Can cost inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation added about INR 125 crore of revenue. Q4 FY26 VAST margin was about 6.5-7%. Most index-linked commodities have back-to-back pass-through with a lag of a quarter or two, and customers are expected to support pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did share of profit from associates and JVs fall from about INR 31 crore to about INR 18 crore, and is the Furukawa contribution recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Flash PAT contribution fell to about INR 18-19 crore from about INR 25 crore in Q4 FY26, due to excess depreciation at Flash. Furukawa contributed INR 80 lakh vs INR 5 crore in Q4. Management called the dip temporary, expecting Flash back on track in one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sunroof SOP for Q2 on track, and what is the status of the passenger vehicle EV motor work at Flash?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunroof (Spark Minda HCMF) product trials were approved first time and the SOP is on track for Q2. Flash has magnet-less motors across segments, some under customer testing, with one PV customer engagement and two or three partnerships pending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the switches order ramp and Flash cross-selling expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Switches lifetime order book exceeds INR 1,000 crore, with SOP in Q1 FY28, about INR 150 crore revenue in FY28 and peak in FY29. Die casting cross-sell for Flash started in August 2026, with wiring harness under testing; no specific INR 50-70 crore figure was confirmed.

risks_watch: Flash EBITDA margin (15.4% in Q1) and whether it recovers to the 16-17% long-term range within one to two quarters as indexation aligns with customers.
Pass-through lag on raw material, freight and wage costs; a one-to-two quarter lag could keep group margin near 11.5% against the 11.5-12% guide.
Flash growth of 20-24% against EV demand and capacity build-out; management said capacity must be added first.
Furukawa and associate share of profit (about INR 18 crore vs INR 31 crore in Q4 FY26): whether the dip is temporary.
Execution timelines: Turntide SOPs (Oct-Nov 2026), sunroof SOP (Q2), switches SOP (Q1 FY28) and the switches ramp to about INR 150 crore in FY28.
Quality of Q1 profit: PAT of INR 206 crore includes a INR 106 crore one-time exceptional gain from VAST consolidation; underlying PAT is much lower.
Vision 2030 target of INR 17,500 crore, disputed by an analyst on the FY30 gap; watch the organic growth rate versus the about 30% cited.
key_quotes: So, this is the same momentum which is expected to continue over the upcoming quarters, going into FY28 as well.
And we are very confident that on a longer -term basis, the company should maintain a margin anywhere between 16% to 17%.
There will be pressure, but given that these are all exceptional times, we have to support customers, customers will also support us.
We believe that Flash will be back on track in the next one or two quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order momentum, and on the Vision 2030 target, but cautious on margins, where management attributes the Q1 pressure to commodity, labour and freight costs and repeatedly frames it as a time lag. Management was evasive on the analyst's FY30 revenue-gap calculation, disputing the figure without offering a bridge, and on the contract-labour question, which it did not answer directly.
